statements.t: We also pursue public transportation projects on a selective basis.

Our current strategic plan, which we began implementing in 2025, is directed at expanding our self-performed mechanical, electrical and civil construction capabilities within our focus markets and competing on the basis of technical capability and cost and schedule performance while maintaining a low-risk portfolio of projects that are within our core competencies.

We perform electrification work for public and private facilities, including projects associated with the transition from fossil fuel-based systems, and we install medium- and low-voltage electrical systems at industrial facilities, ports, airports and other infrastructure sites.
The increase was primarily attributable to our new strategy of expanded bidding activity with a focus on risk-balanced contracts in our target markets.
Our backlog as of October 2, 2026 was concentrated in California, Texas and Washington, with the remainder attributable to projects in four other states.
We expect that our results of operations will be affected by a number of factors which we have discussed below.

These conditions and events can negatively impact our financial results due to, among other things, the termination, deferral or delay of projects, reduced productivity and exposure to significant liabilities.

Typically, our revenue is lowest in the first quarter of the year because cold, snowy or wet conditions can create challenging working environments that are more costly for our customers or cause delays on projects.
In the event of a project cancellation, we may be reimbursed for certain costs, but we typically have no contractual right to the total revenues reflected in our backlog.

Backlog amounts are determined based on target price estimates that incorporate historical trends, anticipated seasonal impacts, experience from similar projects and from communications with our customers.
We selectively bid on projects that we believe offer an opportunity to meet our profitability objectives or that offer the opportunity to enter promising new markets.

We will potentially face strong competition and pricing pressures for any additional contract awards from other government agencies, and we may be required to qualify or continue to qualify under various multiple award task order contract criteria.
For example, we target projects with significant, highly-technical work that we can self-perform.

In addition, as a result of federal and state-level infrastructure initiatives, we believe that funding for technical construction projects may exceed capacity, enabling us to opportunistically target smaller specialized projects with less risk at higher margins.
We primarily compete for new contracts independently, seeking to win and complete new projects directly for our customers.

Our customers primarily award contracts using one of two methods: the traditional public “competitive bid” method, in which price is the major determining factor, or through a “best value” or collaborative contract proposal, where contracts are awarded based on a combination of technical qualifications, proposed project team, schedule, the ability to obtain surety bonds, past performance on similar projects and…
Many of our contracts are awarded on a fixed-price basis, and we earn and recognize revenue using an input measure of total costs incurred divided by total costs expected to be incurred.
We are subject to variation in scope and cost of projects from our original projections.

In certain circumstances, we seek to collect or assert claims against customers, engineers, consultants, subcontractors or others involved in a project for additional costs exceeding the contract price or for amounts not included in the original contract price.
Our costs primarily consist of payroll, equipment, materials, and other project related expenses.
With a consistent focus on profitability by our management team, we leverage information technology and utilize financial systems to improve project execution and control costs.

However, if we are unable to accurately estimate the overall risks, requirements or costs when we bid on or negotiate a contract that is ultimately awarded to us, we may achieve a lower than anticipated profit or incur a loss on the contract.
In addition, the market value of our equipment may unexpectedly decline at a faster rate than anticipated.
We have also implemented the 2023 Omnibus Incentive Plan to align our equity compensation program with public company plans and practices, which increases our stock-based compensation expense.
We participate in various construction joint ventures in order to share expertise, risk and resources for certain highly complex, large, and/or unique projects.

The joint venture agreements typically provide that our interests in any profits and assets, and our respective share in any losses and liabilities, that may result from the performance of the contract are limited to our stated percentage interest in the project.
The sponsoring partner typically provides administrative, accounting and much of the project management support for the project and generally receives a fee from the joint venture for these services.
We have been designated as the sponsoring partner in some venture projects and are a non-sponsoring partner in others.

We have also made an adjustment for transformation costs we have incurred including advisory costs in connection with settling outstanding claims, exiting the Non-Core Projects and transforming the Company to shift our strategy to meet the nation’s growing need for water and other critical infrastructure and grow our business.

However, future cash flows are subject to a number of variables, and significant additional expenditures will be required to conduct our operations.

In the event we make one or more acquisitions and the amount of capital required is greater than the amount we have available for acquisitions at that time, we could be required to reduce the expected level of expenditures and/or seek additional capital.
We cannot guarantee that this additional capital will be available on acceptable terms or at all.

The Company’s operating assets and liabilities fluctuations are impacted by the mix of projects in backlog, seasonality, the timing of new awards and related payments for work performed and the contract billings to the customer as projects are completed.

As construction on our contracts progresses, we increase or decrease backlog to take account of changes in estimated quantities under fixed-price contracts, as well as to reflect changed conditions, change orders and other variations from initially anticipated contract revenue and costs, including completion penalties and bonuses.
As of October 2, 2026, we had a backlog of projects of $907 million.
